questions.question: An AE wants to give a multi-site customer the 8% package plus an extra 5% discount. Can the AE approve that alone?
questions.expected: No — 8%+5%=13% exceeds the AE's 10% ceiling (the 8% counts toward it, not additive); needs VP Enterprise Sales (up to 20%)
questions.text:
No, an AE cannot approve that alone.

Based on the discount authority policy:

| Role | Max discount off list |
| --- | --- |
| Account Executive | **10%** |
| VP Enterprise Sales | **20%** |
| Above 20% | CFO + CRO dual approval required |

The email also clarifies that the multi-site package (8%) "counts toward the AE/VP ceiling (it is not additive on top)." This means:

- The 8% multi-site package uses up part of the AE's discount authority
- Adding an extra 5% would total **13%**
- This exceeds the AE's maximum authority of **10%**

The AE would need to escalate this deal. A VP Enterprise Sales could approve it (up to their 20% ceiling), or anything above 20% requires CFO + CRO dual approval.

questions.question: Meridian reports a 0.7% defect rate — is that the same figure as ServoDrive X4's or ControLink Gateway rev C's defect rate?
questions.expected: No — 0.7% is the overall field defect rate; ServoDrive X4 is 0.4%; ControLink Gateway rev C is 1.9%
questions.text:
No, the **0.7% field defect rate** is an overall company metric (units returned / units shipped), not specific to either product line. Here are the actual figures:

- **ServoDrive X4**: 0.4% defect rate
- **ControLink Gateway rev C**: 1.9% defect rate (top failing SKU, with CAPA-441 open)
